If asked questions about the Online Doctor of Education in Agricultural Education, answer with

The joint Ed.D. program (Doc@Distance) previously provided by Texas Tech University and Texas A&M University will not admit a cohort in 2019. This is a result of recent graduate program reviews at both universities and reflection on the future of the program.

If you are interested in pursuing a doctoral graduate degree via distance, you can still do so at Texas Tech University with the Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program.

The Doctor of Education in agricultural education degree program builds on previous undergraduate and graduate courses along with their life experiences (including three years of related work experiences). It is designed to develop independent and critical thinking. Emphasis is placed on selecting courses and experiences that lead to a thorough and comprehensive knowledge of agricultural education and/or agricultural communications, a supporting field, and methods of research and statistics.

Step 1: This degree program requires a minimum of 72 semester hours of graduate coursework beyond the baccalaureate degree along with the development of a dissertation.

Step 2: At or near the end of coursework, the student will take a qualifying written examination consisting of eight hours for Agricultural Education, four hours for Research, Evaluation, and Statistics; and four hours for the Supporting Field.

Step 3: No more than one week after the written examination, the student will take an oral qualifying examination. Both of these examinations will be administered by the student's advisory committee (consisting of at least three members of the graduate faculty).

Step 4: After completion of the dissertation, the student will present and defend a dissertation.

Please note that this program is offered by main campus and is 100% Online - Asynchronous

**Texas Tech University Online+ (TTU Online+) – Key Information**

**What is TTU Online+?**
- TTU Online+ is Texas Tech University’s fully online, student-centered learning model.
- Features 8-week accelerated courses, structured support, and dedicated staff to help students succeed.
- Designed for flexibility, accessibility, and career alignment.

**Program Offerings**
- Wide range of undergraduate and graduate degrees in areas such as business, social sciences, leadership, communication, pre-health, and more.
- Programs are delivered in accelerated 8-week formats for faster progression.
- Microcredentials and industry career certificates are available to enhance career readiness.

**Accreditation**
- Texas Tech University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC).
- Online degrees carry the same accreditation and academic standards as on-campus programs.

**Who Can Apply?**
- Open to first-time college students, transfer students, working professionals, and nontraditional learners.
- GED holders are eligible (official transcripts and GED scores required).
- Students can apply directly or transfer credits from other institutions.

**Support & Student Experience**
- Personalized support from recruiters, enrollment specialists, academic advisors, and online student advocates.
- Access to tutoring, writing center, technical support, and career counseling.
- Online students are eligible to participate in commencement.

**Course Structure & Flexibility**
- 8-week asynchronous courses (no required live sessions).
- Multiple start dates throughout the year.
- Designed for working adults—study on your schedule from anywhere in the country.

**Financial Aid & Affordability**
- Competitive tuition rates; cost varies by program.
- Eligible students can apply for federal financial aid, scholarships, grants, and military benefits.
- Tuition is charged per credit hour; financial aid is typically disbursed by semester.

**Transfer Credits & Prior Learning**
- Transfer credits are evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
- Free prior learning assessments (PLA) allow students to earn credit for work and life experience.

**How to Apply**
- Applications are completed online: https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/apply/
- Official transcripts from all prior institutions are required.

**Contact & More Information**
- Website: [GoOnline.ttu.edu](http://GoOnline.ttu.edu)
- Phone: 1-844-691-0494
- Email: online@ttu.edu

**Next Steps**
- Explore programs: https://www.depts.ttu.edu/online/programs/
- Contact an enrollment specialist for personalized guidance.

How long does it take to complete an Online+ degree?

Most students complete their Online+ degree in 2-4 years, depending on transfer credits and course load. Our 8-week courses and multiple start dates help you graduate faster.

Comprehensive Evaluation/Comprehensive Examination

All TTU graduate students MUST complete a comprehensive evaluation in order to graduate. There are four (4) different options for students in the CS Dept. to complete this:

Step 1: Master's Thesis

Step 2: Students must publicly defend their completed thesis to satisfy this requirement. Six (6) hours of CS 6000 - Master's Thesis AND CS faculty approval is required.

Step 3: Master's Project

Step 4: Students will complete an oral examination wherein they present publicly on project results. Requires three (3) credit hours of CS 6001 - Master's Project AND CS faculty approval

Step 5: Industry Career Certificate through Coursera

Step 6: Students will complete an approved industry career certificate through Coursera. Students can begin the certificate of their choice from the CS Learning Program as early as their first semester in the program.

Step 7: Work Experience

Step 8: Students can participate in an approved internship/CPT (see grad advisor). The internship/CPT requires co-enrollment in CS 5000 - Practicum in Computer Science

Step 9: Distance students who are working full-time professionals in a relevant industry may ask that their full-time job be considered to satisfy this requirement (see grad advisor).

The CS Dept. no longer offers an exam or report option.

Flexible Learning Schedule

Every student has unique obligations and responsibilities that have an impact on when and where they can engage in learning, but that shouldn't hold them back from earning a graduate degree. That's why you can attend our program as a full-time or part-time student and why most of the curriculum is offered with an asynchronous modality. Students in our online MSW program can mold study time to whatever schedule works best for them, from first thing in the morning all the way to the wee hours of nightime. Whatever time it is, your class materials will be waiting for you. On the other hand, we know from experience that most students want some face-to-face time to get to know their professors and peers, as well as to ask questions and get help. In the TTU Online MSW program, you'll have the option to drop-in during professors' real-time office hours and attend real-time meet-ups at least a few times each semester.

Certifications

Alongside the core curriculum, students will be Microsoft Office Excel Specialist certified upon graduation.

Program format

Our 42 credit-hour program can be completed 100% online, allowing you to maintain professional and personal commitments while obtaining your degree. Full-time students can earn their degree in as little as one year. Part-time students can take classes at a slower pace, earning their degrees in two to six years. Individuals who are employed full-time while in the program typically complete their degree within two years.

**How to Register for Your Online+ Classes**

Follow these steps to register for Online+ classes at Texas Tech University:

1. **Login to Raiderlink**  
   - Go to [Raiderlink](https://raiderlink.ttu.edu) and log in with your eRaider credentials.

2. **Navigate to Registration**  
   - Click on the “MyTech” Tab (located in the red column on the left).
   - Find “Manage My Enrollment” on the main part of the screen.
   - Select “Registration.”

3. **Browse or Add Classes**  
   - To search for classes:  
     - Click “Look Up Classes,” then “Browse Classes.”
     - Select the desired term (Early/Late Fall, Spring, or Summer TTU Online).
     - Use the “Advanced Search” feature to refine your search.
   - To register with a CRN (Course Reference Number):  
     - Click “Add/Drop Classes,” then “Register for Classes.”
     - Select the term you want.
     - Click on the “Enter CRNs” tab and type in the 5-digit CRN(s).
     - Click “Add to Summary,” review your classes, and click “Submit.”
     - You should see a green “Registered” status beside each class if successful.

4. **Check Your Time Ticket**  
   - Make sure your registration window (time ticket) is open.  
   - To find your time ticket:  
     - In Raiderlink, click on "Add or Drop Classes."
     - Click “View Information” to see your assigned registration window.

5. **Finalize Registration**  
   - Review your schedule and confirm your registration is complete.

**Need Help?**
- If you have issues or questions, contact your Online Student Advocate or Advisor.
- For technical support, contact TTU Online+ at 1-844-691-0494 or online@ttu.edu.

The Advanced School Counseling Certificate is designed for professionals who have already earned a master’s degree in counseling and are seeking to become certified school counselors in Texas. Completion of the certificate satisfies the educational and practicum requirements for Texas School Counselor certification through Texas Tech University’s approved Educator Preparation Program. **Full-Time Status and Financial Aid for Online+ Graduate Students**

- For Online+ graduate programs, **6 credit hours per 8-week term** is considered full-time enrollment.
